C2.note: SLD_R and SLD_D coincide on this arm because the single-locus frequencies do not move; that is why A2 cannot decide the normalisation and A1 must

C3.normalisation_verdict: UNDECIDED on this grid -- the two readings are not separated by the error bars. This is a failure of the RUN, not a finding about the corpus.
C3.why_it_matters: ldOverlapFromSharedLD is the identity function, so the corpus never states whether shared_ld is measured on D or on r. Under pure drift D decays like heterozygosity, so the D reading already contains the frequency factor and multiplying by (1-fst) counts drift twice. The two readings differ by exactly (1-fst).
C3.pass_note: pass tracks the INSTRUMENT under the reading the measurement supports. Which reading the DECLARATION should name is the finding above and does not flip READ_THE_TEST.

C4.demonstrates: the joint sweep cannot falsify a product; only the one-at-a-time sweeps can. Measured here, not asserted.

C6.scope_note: DGP.lean states no theorem identifies this chart with a process AUC. The prevalence-independence here is a property of the CHART. fam_metrics measured a liability-threshold AUC moving 0.833 -> 0.925 across prevalence, so this field cannot be the deployed quantity at more than one prevalence. Scope result, not a refuted theorem.
C6.targetR2_not_measured_here: targetR2FromNeutralAFBenchmark forwards to presentDayR2, measured by fam_pgs_transport_drift.py C5. Only the forwarding is checked here, so the quantity is not counted twice.
